title: Sequence packing without document masks: each epoch's shuffled records concatenated into <= 512-token rows (~3 unrelated theorem/proof pairs per row, causal attention across them), token-budget batches of rows, on the 153-claude width-384 Lean incumbent (model unchanged, 9,557,760 params)
description: Idea ID: the packing lead from program.md (data-order scope; no backlog P-number; kin to P34/P32's length-transfer family). The model, optimizer, loss and schedule are 153's byte for byte; only batch construction changes: the epoch's random permutation of training records is packed in order into rows of at most 512 tokens (a record is never split), the rows are length-sorted and cut into the same 18,432-token budget per step, and the shift augmentation is drawn per record inside a row. 146-claude packed WITH document masks (same math as unpacked) and lost on speed (-29% steps); here there is no mask, so a proof's causal attention sees the 1-3 earlier unrelated pairs in its row. Why it should help expert iteration: the RL/eval targets are 7-14 line proofs, longer than every cap-6 training proof, so the sampler must attend over contexts and premise sets it never saw in pretraining; packed rows train the ALiBi heads on 400-512-token contexts and force the NoPE content-lookup heads to pick the right premise among distractor hypotheses and reused names (two pairs in a row can both have an n3), the skill a long proof with many candidate lines needs. bench_pretrain (probe): 9.87 steps/s vs 10.74-11.53 for the incumbent code, so ~10% fewer steps.
hypothesis: Since 100 the Lean-protocol keeps that were not capacity were length-transfer mechanisms (ALiBi +19, hybrid ALiBi/NoPE +25) and the RL start (round-1 targets solved) is where recent candidates won or lost (153: 736 mean; 159-fable3: 625). Pretraining at this budget is data-limited and overfits by ~150 s (val minima 0.069-0.078 then rising to 0.088 while train reaches 0.054), so the marginal step teaches little about single short proofs; packing turns the same tokens into a harder task on the same records: predict each proof with 0-3 unrelated theorem/proof pairs and their hypothesis names in the causal context. Mechanism 1 (positional): ALiBi heads see query-key distances up to ~500 during training instead of <= 537 only for the rarest records, so the slope/decay is calibrated on long ranges when eval proofs run past 300 tokens. Mechanism 2 (content): NoPE heads must localize the current pair's hypotheses and lines among distractors, so retrieval by content alone is penalized and 'recent, same-pair' evidence is learned, which is what a 12-line proof citing among 11 earlier lines needs; the paper-level analogue is that packing without masks acts as an in-context distractor regularizer (this is the standard GPT-2/3 training regime). Predicted effect: equal or slightly worse val loss on single records, better round-1 sampler on long targets, gain concentrated at >= 9. Risks: (a) train/test mismatch, since at sampling every proof starts at position 0 with no preceding pair, while in training only ~31% of records do; (b) regularizer-like interventions have consistently lost here (drop-path -49, attention dropout -16, curriculum -39), and cross-pair context is noise the model must learn to ignore; (c) the ~10% step cost (bench 9.87 vs 10.74-11.53 steps/s) at a recipe where -29% steps cost -79 (146) and -32% cost -31 (147). Falsifiers: steps mean < 3,500 (packing is not cheap); round-1 targets solved mean < 650 (the distractor context hurt the start); final single-record val loss > 0.100 on two seeds (the model could not ignore cross-pair context).
expected_delta: -45 to +40 theorems at >=7 (3-seed mean), central +4; keep needs > 687.00 (153-claude: 676/700/685). Mechanism predictions: pretraining steps 3,700-4,300 per seed (central ~3,970 = 153's 4,503 x the bench ratio 9.87/11.2; 153: 4540/4479/4489), falsified as 'cheap' if the mean is < 3,500; records_seen/epochs 3.3-3.9 (rows_per_epoch ~40-48k, batches_per_epoch ~1,000-1,150); final single-record val loss 0.080-0.098 (153: 0.088/0.087/0.089; the bench probe was 0.081 at 60 s vs 153 seed 0's 0.087) with train loss 0.050-0.062 (153: 0.054-0.060); post-pretrain held-out greedy 0.955-0.975 (153: 0.9675/0.967/0.968); round-1 RL targets solved 650-820 (153: 766/747/694) and round-1 sample acc 0.20-0.32; round-4 RL-solved 1,110-1,210 (153: 1157/1168/1191); deep bins >= 10 at 100-130 (153: 109/107/107), >= 11 at 20-32 (153: 26/22/23), with any metric gain expected to come disproportionately from >= 9; RL sampling >= 190 samples/s in round 1 (153: 225/227/200; model identical); totals 1,650-2,100 s (153: 1725/1741/1664); n_params 9,557,760 exactly.

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) ALiBiGPT with Peri-LN blocks and hybrid ALiBi/NoPE heads, unchanged from 151-claude except width; PeriLNBlock now replaces the fork Block's 4*D fc1/fc2 with Linear(D, D_FF)/Linear(D_FF, D), D_FF = 1280 (same as 151's 4*320)
arch.pos: hybrid alibi/nope (unchanged from 115-fable): no rotation of q/k in any block; additive per-head bias -slope_h * (query position - key position) on the scaled attention logits via SDPA attn_mask, slopes 2^(-8h/4) = 1/4, 1/16, 1/64, 1/256 for heads 1..4 (Press et al. 2021 standard set for 4 heads) and 0 for heads 5..8 (bias identically 0 except -inf for masked/future keys, i.e. NoPE heads); same slope table in every block; -inf for masked/future keys
arch.norm: layernorm (pre-LN on branch inputs + LayerNorm on attention and MLP branch outputs, Peri-LN, unchanged from 107)
arch.change: vs 153-claude: none. ALiBiGPT/PeriLNBlock, 6 blocks x width 384, 8 heads of 48 (4 ALiBi slopes 1/4..1/256 + 4 NoPE), d_ff 1280, Peri-LN, MTP module, Muon/AdamW split, schedule, init and handoff are byte-identical to 153's pretrain.py; the only change is how each step's batch is built (packed rows, see batch/data). n_params 9,557,760 as in 153 (bench_pretrain reported the same).
arch.n_params_detail: model: 9,557,760 (CPU check with fork 51604b3, vocab 107; bench_pretrain on an A40 reported the same; per Peri-LN block 1,579,136 = qkv 443,520 + proj 147,840 + fc1 492,800 + fc2 491,904 + 4 LayerNorms 3,072; emb + head 82,176; ln_f 768). MTP module (pretraining only, never registered on the model, dropped at handoff as since 136-fable): 1,875,584; pretraining trains 11,433,344 in total, so unlike 151 the total is over 10M if the discarded MTP module were counted; the harness caps the handed-off model's parameters (9.56M), which is what RL and eval use
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 384, 8) from this pretrain.py with PeriLNBlock blocks (d_ff 1280), then load state; the MTP module is not saved and not needed for inference
arch.kv_cache: unchanged (caches[0] holds key positions); CPU check cached vs full forward max abs logit diff 1.4e-6 at width 384

tokenizer.source: fork 51604b3 lean_tok.LeanTokenizer('lean_seq') via tokenizer.make_tokenizer; Lean 4 have-chain text, names n1..n64 numbered by first appearance

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale) with Polar Express orthogonalization on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight; AdamW on embeddings, biases and LayerNorms; the MTP module's five 2D matrices (block qkv split into Q/K/V, block proj, fc1, fc2, and the (384,768) input proj) join Muon and its LayerNorms/biases join AdamW (unchanged from 151)
optimizer.schedule: cosine over wall-clock, unchanged from 129/151: after the 200-step linear warmup, lr = 1e-3 * (0.3 + 0.35 * (1 + cos(pi * frac))), frac = elapsed / budget, ending at 0.3 x peak; Muon lr = 0.01 * lr / 1e-3 and its decoupled decay follow the same factor

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(rows, columns) / D) with D = 384 per orthogonalized matrix (RMS-matched, Moonshot convention with its 0.2 constant folded into MUON_LR): Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 (1280,384) and fc2 (384,1280) sqrt(1280/384) = 1.83, head (107,384) 1, MTP proj (384,768) sqrt(2); MUON_LR 0.01 unchanged
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW (floor 0.3, unchanged); muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: 6 x (qkv.weight (1152,384) split into Q/K/V, proj, fc1, fc2) plus head.weight, plus the MTP module's 5 matrices: 30 Muon matrices as in 148/151 (CPU check: muon_step runs over all 30)
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: unchanged: each QKV update reshaped to (3,384,384), orthogonalized per role; fc1 (1280,384) is not (3D, D) so it is orthogonalized whole
muon.coefficients_note: per-iteration Polar Express quintic coefficients (Amsel, Persson, Musco, Gower 2025; values as in modded-nanogpt, num_iters=5, safety factor 2e-2, cushion 2) replace Keller Jordan's fixed (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) used five times. Same five iterations (two matmuls each on the Gram side plus one), same bf16 precision, same transpose/QKV-split/shape-scale handling.
muon.normalization: update / (Frobenius norm * 1.02 + 1e-6) (Polar Express safety factor) instead of update / (Frobenius norm + 1e-7)
muon.local_check: CPU check (float64 scalar map over sigma in [1e-3,1]): output singular values in [0.847,1.141] vs fixed quintic [0.471,1.202]; for sigma>=3e-3 [0.859,1.141] vs [0.682,1.202]. bf16 torch on random (256,256)/(1024,256)/(99,256) matrices: median singular value 0.94/0.95/1.02 vs 0.75/0.77/0.77, update RMS +14%/+14%/+19%.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (ln1, ln2, + ln_attn_out, ln_mlp_out per block, and ln_f); head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW. The new output-LayerNorm gains and biases get the same AdamW lr 1e-3 and wd 0.1 as every other LayerNorm
optimizer.decay_convention: unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1, so Muon per-step shrinkage lr*0.1 is ten times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 (peak 1e-3 per step), applied to all 25 Muon matrices including head.weight; AdamW group decay wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3. Note: with output LayerNorms, Muon weight decay on proj/fc2 no longer shrinks a branch's residual write (the LayerNorm re-normalizes it); only the AdamW-decayed output gains set that scale. Because decay is lr-scaled, the higher floor raises late-training per-step decay (endpoint 3x 115's); MUON_WD itself is unchanged at 0.1
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 over model.parameters() + the MTP module's parameters, before both optimizers (unchanged)
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; the MTP module and both pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW on model.parameters()
optimizer.parameters: 24 trunk hidden matrices + head.weight, plus the MTP module's qkv (split), proj, fc1, fc2 and input proj (384,768): 30 Muon matrices during pretraining; the handoff model's parameters are 9,557,760

batch.padding: rows padded with the pad token to the longest row in the batch (gathered from an appended all-pad dummy record); rows fill to ~433 of 512 tokens (mean) and stable length-sorting keeps batches near-homogeneous, so fill is ~100% (18,088 of 18,088 slots in the CPU check); a row longer than 512 tokens is a single record (max 537)
batch.change: vs 153-claude: the unit of a batch is a packed row of consecutive records from the epoch permutation (greedy in-order first-fit into <= 512 tokens, never splitting a record; ~3.2 records per row, ~44k rows per epoch of ~140k records), instead of a single record. Rows are then stably sorted by length and cut into runs with count * max_len <= 18,432 exactly as 148/153 did with records, run order shuffled with random.Random(seed). Tokens per step (~18k real) and records per step (~135) are therefore unchanged; what changes is that every record after the first in a row is preceded by 1-3 unrelated theorem/proof pairs that its causal attention can see (no document mask). CPU gather cost ~0.7 ms per step.
batch.size_note: variable: one token-budget cut of packed rows, count * max_row_len <= 18,432; on a synthetic length distribution matching mean ~135 / max 537 that is 11..64 rows per step, mean ~42 rows = ~135 records (153: ~136 records per step)

data.augmentation: random name start offset (lean_seq n1..n64) drawn independently per record inside a packed row (same distribution as 153's per-record shift; two records in one row can therefore reuse the same names for different hypotheses)
data.order: shuffle at the record level each epoch (GPU generator, seed); records packed in permutation order into rows of <= 512 tokens; rows stably length-sorted into token-budget batches whose order is shuffled. Data-order change: a proof's context now contains ~2 earlier, unrelated theorem/proof pairs on average (0 for the first record of a row, i.e. ~31% of records); all records stay in play, none dropped, no new records or text.

config.init: unchanged rule from 148/151: fork _init (normal 0.02 embedding/readout, zero biases), orthogonal_ on every 2D block and MTP parameter with gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols)), so element std stays 0.02 at width 384; LayerNorm gain 1, bias 0

loss.main: the fork's loss_on: next-token cross-entropy on proof-token positions (unchanged; val_loss and the recorded train_loss/last_loss use this term only, so they stay comparable with 129)
loss.mtp: DeepSeek-V3 (2024) sequential multi-token prediction, depth 1 (Gloeckle et al. 2024 style shared head): z_t = proj(cat(LN(h_t), LN(emb(x_{t+1})))) for t in 0..T-3, one Peri-LN causal block over z with the same ALiBi/NoPE bias sliced to T-2 positions, then the model's ln_f and head predict x_{t+2}; cross-entropy masked to proof-token targets (m[:, 2:]), mean over those positions
loss.total: main + MTP_WEIGHT * mtp with MTP_WEIGHT = 0.3 constant over the whole budget (DeepSeek-V3's early-training value); curve points also record the mean recent mtp loss as mtp_loss
loss.leakage_check: CPU check: perturbing token x[7] changes the MTP block's outputs only at positions 6..9 (which read emb(x[7]) or later), never at position 5 whose target is x[7]
loss.packing: the fork's loss_on/mtp_loss are unchanged: targets are masked to proof-token positions, so a pair's prompt tokens (including the first token after the previous pair's last proof token) are never predicted; each pair's proof tokens are predicted with the whole row prefix as context. val_loss is still computed on the 1,024 held-out single records (unpacked), so it stays comparable with 153.

config.bench: bench_pretrain.py --secs 60 on one A40 (probe, not evidence): 595 steps in 60.3 s = 9.87 steps/s (incumbent 153 code on other pods: 695/11.53, 690/11.44, 647/10.74, so ~8-14% step cost from the ~3x longer attention rows), peak 7.42 GB (153: 7.42), n_params 9,557,760, val loss 0.0811 at 60 s / 595 steps (153 seed 0: 0.0870 at 60 s / 716 steps), sampling 264 samples/s (model identical to 153; pod variance), sample_acc 0.0146 after 60 s
